title: Canonical modules on normal surface modifications
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], with a normalized algebraic dualizing complex $\Omega_A$ [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Then $\Omega_A\cong\omega_A[2]$ for a finitely generated torsion-free $A$-module $\omega_A$ of rank one [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; rank one means $\omega_A\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}A\cong\operatorname{Frac}A$, and torsion-free means that multiplication by any nonzero element of $A$ is injective. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper and induce an isomorphism of function fields, with $X$ integral, normal, Noetherian and of dimension $2$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The relative dualizing complex $f^!\widetilde\Omega_A$ is $\omega_X[2]$, where $\omega_X$ is a coherent torsion-free $\mathcal O_X$-module of generic rank one [pqf-def-coherent]. Here $f^!$ is the right adjoint of ordinary derived pushforward on the derived categories of structure-sheaf modules with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $[2]$ is cohomological shift [def-pc-derived-category]. For every $x\in X$, the module $\omega_{X,x}$ has finite injective dimension over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, meaning it admits an injective resolution of finite length [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If $x$ is closed and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=2$, then $\omega_{X,x}[2]$ is a normalized algebraic dualizing complex for $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Compatibilities: (a) if $X'$ also satisfies the hypotheses on $X$ and $g:X'\to X$ is a proper morphism with $f\circ g$ the structure morphism of $X'$, then $\omega_{X'}[2]\cong g^!(\omega_X[2])$, where $g^!$ is the right adjoint of derived pushforward along $g$. (b) In the situation of (a), let $x\in X$ be closed with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=2$, put $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with the normalized algebraic dualizing complex $\Omega_B=\omega_{X,x}[2]$, and let $g_B:X'_B=X'\times_X\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $B$, $\Omega_B$ and $g_B$ satisfy the hypotheses above in place of $A$, $\Omega_A$ and $f$, and the restriction of $\omega_{X'}$ to $X'_B$ is the module $\omega_{X'_B}$ attached to $g_B$ and $\Omega_B$.
